title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 71
paragraphs: Yet every means had been taken to prevent the barbarians from entering the Peloponnese by land. As soon as the Peloponnesians heard that Leonidas and his company had perished at Thermopylae, they quickly gathered from their cities and took up position at the Isthmus, and over them was set as commander Cleombrotos, son of Anaxandrides and brother of Leonidas. Posted at the Isthmus, they had destroyed the Skironian way, and after this (having so decided in council) they began building a wall across the Isthmus. Being many tens of thousands, with every man joining in the work, it proceeded fast: stones, bricks, timbers, and baskets of sand were brought to it continually, and those who had come to help never paused in their labor either by night or by day.
